newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's M6 comes top in TV image study.
newsitem.headline: France's M6 comes top in TV image study.

text.p: French private television station M6-Metropole Television is rated as the most popular general channel, overtaking its bigger and older rivals, according to a six-monthly survey published by advertising weekly Strategies on Friday.
The survey, the eighth barometer of television channels' image carried out by polling institute BVA for Strategies, showed a stable score for public channels France 2 and France 3.
It found 47 percent of those questioned saw an improvement in programmes at M6, which is owned by Lyonnaise des Eaux and CLT-Audiofina, while 15 percent said programmes had deteriorated.
TF1, France's biggest private channel, and pay TV station Canal Plus, were both criticised by the television viewers questioned, Strategies said.
Regular TF1 viewers found the quality of its programmes had improved, but those who watched it occasionally said the opposite.

Regular Canal Plus viewers thought its programmes had deteriorated, a situation Strategies said was serious for the encrypted channel, whose image has been declining consistently over the last four years according to the survey.

The arrival this year of new digital satellite television services in France, notably TF1's Television par Satellite (TPS), erodes Canal Plus's previous near-monopoly on the French pay television market.
The favourite channel was publicly-owned Arte, a Franco-German cultural and intellectual station, but over half those interviewed expressed no opinion on its programmes, Strategies said.

The arrival of digital satellite services in France has triggered a strong level of interest, with 65 percent of those questioned having heard of TPS six months after its launch -- a score identical to that registered by Canal Plus's Canalsatellite digital service six months after it hit the airwaves.
Nearly a quarter had heard of their smaller rival, AB Productions' ABSat, whose channels are less widely available, Strategies said.
In France only five percent had never heard of satellite television, according to the survey. Three percent had signed up for satellite services, while 10 percent were cable subscribers.
The best-known channel available on cable and satellite services was Eurosport, with 39 percent having heard of it and 26 percent having watched it.

Second place, but well below Eurosport's score, was taken by Canal Plus's Canal Jimmy, with 22 percent recognition and 11 percent having watched the channel, which specialises in quality American and British series, humour and music.
